en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn the language of rules, recommendations and formal offers: It is essential that he be on time, I suggest she attend, Should you need any help… Let's start!

steps.title: Rules and requirements
steps.text: You know **were** for unreal things (*If I were you…*, *I wish I were…*). Formal English has another special form, for **rules and requirements**.
steps.body:
The **subjunctive** here = the **base form** of the verb (no -s, no -ed, no *to*), after **essential, vital, important, crucial, necessary** + *that*:
- *It is essential that he **be** on time.* (not *is*)
- *It is vital that each team **submit** its report by Friday.*
**be** for every person. Negative: **not** + base form (*that he **not be** late*). Passive: **be** + third form (*that all forms **be signed***).
British English also says *that he **should** attend* or *that he attends*: fine. Wrong: *that he **will** be*, *that he **to** be*.

steps.title: Rules at work and on campus
steps.text: Here are some real rules. Look at the verb after *that* each time.
steps.body: *wear, submit, be tested, not be interrupted, receive*: no -s, even after *every visitor* or *each school*, and no change after the past *was*. Indonesian *agar / supaya* has no tense, so don't add *will* or *to*.

examples.en: It is essential that every visitor wear a helmet on the construction site.
examples.id: Setiap tamu wajib memakai helm di lokasi proyek.

examples.en: The ministry requires that each school submit its data by 30 June.
examples.id: Kementerian mewajibkan setiap sekolah menyerahkan datanya paling lambat 30 Juni.

examples.en: It is vital that the new payroll system be tested before January.
examples.id: Sistem penggajian yang baru harus diuji sebelum Januari.

examples.en: It is important that the speaker not be interrupted.
It was crucial that the auditor receive the files on time.
examples.id: Waktu itu sangat penting auditor menerima berkasnya tepat waktu.

steps.title: The company handbook
steps.text: Bu Ani from HR is writing the new employee handbook (buku panduan karyawan).

question.prompt: Complete the policy: It is essential that every new employee ___ the safety induction before their first shift.
options: will complete
to complete
complete
question.explanation: After **essential that**, formal English uses the **subjunctive**: the base form, with no -s even after *every new employee*. *will* and *to* are never used in this pattern.

steps.title: suggest, recommend, insist
steps.text: Verbs that **ask for something** use the same base form.
steps.body:
**suggest / recommend / insist / demand / propose (that)** + person + **base form**:
- *I suggest (that) she **attend** the briefing.*
- *Bu Ani insisted that the report **be** sent today.*
The base form stays after a past verb: *He suggested that Rina **lead** the team.*
No person? **suggest / recommend + -ing**: *I suggest **leaving** early.*
Trap: *menyarankan dia **untuk*** → 'I suggest **her to** attend' ✗. *suggest* never takes person + *to*. (British: *I suggest she **attends*** is fine too.)

steps.title: A new colleague
steps.text: Dimas has just joined a startup in Surabaya. His manager writes to the team leader about his first week.

options: I suggest him to shadow Sari for a week.
I suggest that he shadow Sari for a week.
I suggest to him shadow Sari for a week.
question.explanation: **suggest (that) + person + base form**: *that he shadow* (no -s: it's the subjunctive). 'suggest **him to**' is the classic mistake from *menyarankan dia untuk*, and 'suggest **to him** shadow' isn't English.

steps.title: A strict finance manager
steps.text: Last month a wrong invoice cost the company Rp40 million. Since then, Pak Hasan has been very strict.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Pak Hasan bersikeras agar setiap faktur diperiksa.
question.solution: Pak Hasan insisted that every invoice be checked.
question.explanation: **insist that** + **base form**. The invoices are checked by someone, so it's passive: **be + third form** (*be checked*). The base form *be* doesn't change, even after the past *insisted*.

steps.title: The formal were
steps.text: Now the other subjunctive form: **were**. You've used it since B1: *If I were you, I'd…*
steps.body:
**were** = something **unreal**, for every person. Formal writing prefers it to *was*:
- *If the manager **were** less busy, he would reply himself.*
Two formal phrases:
- **as it were** = *kalau boleh dibilang, ibaratnya*: it warns that your words are an image, not literal: *Our IT team is, **as it were**, the engine room of the company.*
- **were it not for** + noun = *kalau bukan karena*: a phrase to remember (its word order is an inversion, a later lesson).
*as it were* ≠ *as it was* (the normal past).

pairs.en: If I were in your position, …

pairs.id: Kalau dia ada di sini, … (tapi tidak)

steps.title: A figure of speech
steps.text: At a conference in Yogyakarta, a speaker talks about a small village library.

question.prompt: 'This library is, as it were, the village's window to the world.' What does 'as it were' tell you?
options: The speaker is using an image, not literal words.
The library was like this in the past, but not now.
The speaker isn't sure the library exists.
question.explanation: **as it were** (= *so to speak, ibaratnya*) is a fixed phrase with the formal **were**: it warns that *window to the world* is an image. It isn't about the past: that would be *as it was*.

steps.title: Polite offers: Should you…
steps.text: Last pattern: the most formal way to offer help at the end of an email.
steps.body:
**Should + subject + base form** = **If** (formal, polite):
- *If you have any questions, …* → ***Should you have** any questions, please contact us.*
- ***Should the flight be** delayed, we will inform you by SMS.*
Use it in HR emails, hotel messages and official letters.
Trap: here **should ≠ seharusnya**: it means *apabila*.
After *Should you*, the **base form**: 'Should you **needed**' ✗, 'Should you **to need**' ✗; and never '**If should** you' ✗.

pairs.en: please do not hesitate to contact us

steps.title: An email to international students
steps.text: Dr. Wulan's assistant is writing to international students about their visa documents.

options: Should you required any further documents, please contact the faculty office.
Should you require any further documents, please contact the faculty office.
If should you require any further documents, please contact the faculty office.
question.explanation: **Should + you + base form** (*require*) = *If you require*, very formal. *required* is the classic mistake (after *should*, always the base form), and *if* and *should* are never used together here.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page. Keep it for your next formal email, report or policy!

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Subjunctive & formal structures
artifact.intro: The subjunctive is the base form (no -s, no -ed, no to) after words of necessity and demand, plus were for unreal situations. Should + subject + base form makes a formal 'if'.
rows: essential / vital / important / necessary that + base form
It is essential that he be on time.
It is important that he not be late.
It is vital that all forms be signed.
It was crucial that the auditor receive the files.
that + should + base form / normal present
that he should attend / that he attends
suggest / recommend / insist / demand (that) + person + base form
I suggest (that) she attend the briefing.
If I were in your position, I'd accept.
She is, as it were, the bridge between the teams.
were it not for + noun (phrase to remember)
Were it not for her help, I'd still be lost.
Should you have any questions, please contact us.
tips: **No -s, no to, no will** after words of necessity: *that she attend*, not *to attend* or *will attend*.
**suggest + person + to** ✗ → *suggest (that) she attend* or *suggest attending*.
In *Should you …*, **should = apabila**, not *seharusnya*; then the base form: *Should you need*, never *Should you needed*.

examples.en: The committee proposed that the deadline be extended.
examples.id: Panitia mengusulkan agar tenggat waktunya diperpanjang.

examples.en: Should there be any changes to the schedule, we will let you know.
examples.id: Apabila ada perubahan jadwal, kami akan memberi tahu Anda.

examples.en: If it were up to me, we would hire her.
examples.id: Kalau keputusannya di tangan saya, kita akan merekrut dia.

steps.text: Want more? Read the British Council C1 page on reporting verbs (with the subjunctive and two tests), and watch two video lessons on the subjunctive from engVid and Anglo-Link.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu akan belajar bahasa untuk aturan, rekomendasi dan tawaran formal: It is essential that he be on time, I suggest she attend, Should you need any help… Ayo mulai!

steps.title: Aturan dan syarat
steps.text: Kamu sudah kenal **were** untuk hal yang tidak nyata (*If I were you…*, *I wish I were…*). Bahasa Inggris formal punya bentuk khusus lagi, untuk **aturan dan syarat**.
steps.body:
**Subjunctive** di sini = **bentuk dasar** kata kerja (tanpa -s, tanpa -ed, tanpa *to*), setelah **essential, vital, important, crucial, necessary** + *that*:
- *It is essential that he **be** on time.* (bukan *is*)
- *It is vital that each team **submit** its report by Friday.*
**be** untuk semua orang. Negatif: **not** + bentuk dasar (*that he **not be** late*). Pasif: **be** + bentuk ketiga (*that all forms **be signed***).
Bahasa Inggris Britania juga memakai *that he **should** attend* atau *that he attends*: boleh. Yang salah: *that he **will** be*, *that he **to** be*.

steps.title: Aturan di kantor dan kampus
steps.text: Ini beberapa aturan sungguhan. Perhatikan kata kerja setelah *that* di setiap kalimat.
steps.body: *wear, submit, be tested, not be interrupted, receive*: tanpa -s, walaupun subjeknya *every visitor* atau *each school*, dan tidak berubah setelah *was* (past). *agar / supaya* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak punya tense, jadi jangan tambahkan *will* atau *to*.

examples.en: It is essential that every visitor wear a helmet on the construction site.
examples.id: Setiap tamu wajib memakai helm di lokasi proyek.

examples.en: The ministry requires that each school submit its data by 30 June.
examples.id: Kementerian mewajibkan setiap sekolah menyerahkan datanya paling lambat 30 Juni.

examples.en: It is vital that the new payroll system be tested before January.
examples.id: Sistem penggajian yang baru harus diuji sebelum Januari.

examples.en: It is important that the speaker not be interrupted.
It was crucial that the auditor receive the files on time.
examples.id: Waktu itu sangat penting auditor menerima berkasnya tepat waktu.

steps.title: Buku panduan perusahaan
steps.text: Bu Ani dari HR sedang menulis buku panduan karyawan yang baru (employee handbook).

question.prompt: Lengkapi kebijakannya: It is essential that every new employee ___ the safety induction before their first shift.
options: will complete
to complete
complete
question.explanation: Setelah **essential that**, bahasa Inggris formal memakai **subjunctive**: bentuk dasar, tanpa -s walaupun subjeknya *every new employee*. *will* dan *to* tidak pernah dipakai dalam pola ini.

steps.title: suggest, recommend, insist
steps.text: Kata kerja yang **meminta sesuatu** memakai bentuk dasar yang sama.
steps.body:
**suggest / recommend / insist / demand / propose (that)** + orang + **bentuk dasar**:
- *I suggest (that) she **attend** the briefing.*
- *Bu Ani insisted that the report **be** sent today.*
Bentuk dasarnya tetap setelah kata kerja past: *He suggested that Rina **lead** the team.*
Tidak ada orangnya? **suggest / recommend + -ing**: *I suggest **leaving** early.*
Jebakan: *menyarankan dia **untuk*** → 'I suggest **her to** attend' ✗. *suggest* tidak pernah diikuti orang + *to*. (Britania: *I suggest she **attends*** juga boleh.)

steps.title: Rekan kerja baru
steps.text: Dimas baru bergabung dengan sebuah startup di Surabaya. Manajernya menulis ke ketua tim tentang minggu pertamanya.

options: I suggest him to shadow Sari for a week.
I suggest that he shadow Sari for a week.
I suggest to him shadow Sari for a week.
question.explanation: **suggest (that) + orang + bentuk dasar**: *that he shadow* (tanpa -s: ini subjunctive). 'suggest **him to**' adalah kesalahan klasik dari *menyarankan dia untuk*, dan 'suggest **to him** shadow' bukan bahasa Inggris.

steps.title: Manajer keuangan yang tegas
steps.text: Bulan lalu satu faktur yang salah membuat perusahaan rugi Rp40 juta. Sejak itu, Pak Hasan sangat ketat.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Pak Hasan bersikeras agar setiap faktur diperiksa.
question.solution: Pak Hasan insisted that every invoice be checked.
question.explanation: **insist that** + **bentuk dasar**. Fakturnya diperiksa oleh seseorang, jadi kalimatnya pasif: **be + bentuk ketiga** (*be checked*). Bentuk dasar *be* tidak berubah, walaupun *insisted* berbentuk past.

steps.title: were yang formal
steps.text: Sekarang bentuk subjunctive yang lain: **were**. Kamu sudah memakainya sejak B1: *If I were you, I'd…*
steps.body:
**were** = sesuatu yang **tidak nyata**, untuk semua orang. Tulisan formal lebih memilihnya daripada *was*:
- *If the manager **were** less busy, he would reply himself.*
Dua frasa formal:
- **as it were** = *kalau boleh dibilang, ibaratnya*: memberi tanda bahwa kata-katamu kiasan, bukan arti harfiah: *Our IT team is, **as it were**, the engine room of the company.*
- **were it not for** + kata benda = *kalau bukan karena*: frasa tetap untuk diingat (susunan katanya inversi, pelajaran nanti).
*as it were* ≠ *as it was* (past biasa).

pairs.en: If I were in your position, …

pairs.id: Kalau dia ada di sini, … (tapi tidak)

steps.title: Kiasan
steps.text: Di sebuah konferensi di Yogyakarta, seorang pembicara bercerita tentang perpustakaan desa yang kecil.

question.prompt: 'This library is, as it were, the village's window to the world.' Apa yang ditunjukkan oleh 'as it were'?
options: The speaker is using an image, not literal words.
The library was like this in the past, but not now.
The speaker isn't sure the library exists.
question.explanation: **as it were** (= *so to speak, ibaratnya*) adalah frasa tetap dengan **were** formal: memberi tanda bahwa *window to the world* adalah kiasan. Frasa ini tidak membicarakan masa lalu: itu *as it was*.
displayOptions: Pembicara memakai gambaran kiasan, bukan makna harfiah.
Perpustakaan dahulu seperti itu, tetapi sekarang tidak lagi.

steps.title: Tawaran sopan: Should you…
steps.text: Pola terakhir: cara paling formal menawarkan bantuan di akhir email.
steps.body:
**Should + subjek + bentuk dasar** = **If** (formal, sopan):
- *If you have any questions, …* → ***Should you have** any questions, please contact us.*
- ***Should the flight be** delayed, we will inform you by SMS.*
Pakai di email HR, pesan hotel dan surat resmi.
Jebakan: di sini **should ≠ seharusnya**: artinya *apabila*.
Setelah *Should you*, pakai **bentuk dasar**: 'Should you **needed**' ✗, 'Should you **to need**' ✗; dan jangan pernah '**If should** you' ✗.

pairs.en: please do not hesitate to contact us

steps.title: Email untuk mahasiswa internasional
steps.text: Asisten Dr. Wulan sedang menulis email untuk mahasiswa internasional tentang dokumen visa mereka.

options: Should you required any further documents, please contact the faculty office.
Should you require any further documents, please contact the faculty office.
If should you require any further documents, please contact the faculty office.
question.explanation: **Should + you + bentuk dasar** (*require*) = *If you require*, sangat formal. *required* adalah kesalahan klasik (setelah *should*, selalu bentuk dasar), dan *if* dan *should* tidak pernah dipakai bersamaan di sini.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk email, laporan atau kebijakan formalmu berikutnya!

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Subjunctive & struktur formal
artifact.intro: Subjunctive adalah bentuk dasar (tanpa -s, tanpa -ed, tanpa to) setelah kata-kata keharusan dan tuntutan, ditambah were untuk situasi yang tidak nyata. Should + subjek + bentuk dasar membentuk 'if' yang formal.
rows: essential / vital / important / necessary that + bentuk dasar
It is essential that he be on time.
It is important that he not be late.
It is vital that all forms be signed.
It was crucial that the auditor receive the files.
that + should + bentuk dasar / present biasa
that he should attend / that he attends
suggest / recommend / insist / demand (that) + orang + bentuk dasar
I suggest (that) she attend the briefing.
If I were in your position, I'd accept.
She is, as it were, the bridge between the teams.
were it not for + kata benda (frasa tetap)
Were it not for her help, I'd still be lost.
Should you have any questions, please contact us.
tips: **Tanpa -s, tanpa to, tanpa will** setelah kata-kata keharusan: *that she attend*, bukan *to attend* atau *will attend*.
**suggest + orang + to** ✗ → *suggest (that) she attend* atau *suggest attending*.
Di *Should you …*, **should = apabila**, bukan *seharusnya*; lalu bentuk dasar: *Should you need*, jangan *Should you needed*.
